papers.title: XenoMix: Estimating mouse content from DNA methylation data of Patient-Derived Xenograft models
papers.summary: Abstract Summary DNA methylation microarrays enable cost-effective, high-throughput profiling of human and mouse samples and are widely used to study epigenetic alterations in cancer. Patient-Derived Xenograft (PDX) models complement this approach by preserving primary tumor characteristics while enabling in vivo studies of drug response and therapy resistance. However, it remains difficult to quantify mouse DNA contamination in PDX DNA methylation data generated using microarrays. We present XenoMix, a light-weight computational tool for quantifying mouse DNA contamination directly from DNA methylation data in PDX models. XenoMix leverages the high sequence homology between human and mouse genomes to detect and quantify unexpected signal contributions originating from mouse DNA. Using ground truth mixtures, XenoMix achieved Pearson’s correlation coefficients higher than 0.99. When applied to PDX data, we identified varying levels of mouse contamination originating from biological and technological variability. XenoMix establishes a critical quality control step in DNA methylation analysis of PDX models, and we show that the estimated contamination can be incorporated as a confounding variable in downstream analyses. Availability and Implementation XenoMix is available as a standalone R package from https://git.dkfz.de/b370/scepigen/XenoMix and as a module in the RnBeads software package

papers.llm_rss_summary_zh:
摘要：DNA甲基化微阵列技术能够以低成本、高通量的方式分析人类和小鼠样本，因此在研究癌症中的表观遗传变化方面得到了广泛应用。患者来源的异种移植模型则通过保留原发肿瘤的特性，使得在体内环境中研究药物反应及治疗耐药性成为可能。然而，在利用微阵列技术生成的PDX DNA甲基化数据中，仍难以准确量化小鼠DNA带来的干扰。我们开发了XenoMix这一轻量级计算工具，它能够直接从PDX模型中的DNA甲基化数据中检测并量化小鼠DNA的污染程度。该工具利用人类与小鼠基因组之间的高度序列相似性，有效识别那些源自小鼠DNA的异常信号。通过使用已知混合样本进行验证，XenoMix的预测结果与实际值之间的皮尔逊相关系数均高于0.99。在实际应用中，我们发现不同PDX样本中的小鼠DNA污染程度存在差异，这些差异可能与生物学因素或技术操作误差有关。XenoMix为PDX模型的DNA甲基化分析提供了重要的质量控制手段；同时，我们证明这些被检测出的污染数据完全可以作为混杂变量纳入后续的分析过程中。

all_papers.summary: Regulatory T (Treg) cells maintain immunological tolerance, but the cellular niches sustaining them across tissues are poorly defined. Work now identifies T follicular helper cells as a source of IL-2 that supports Treg cells in gut-associated lymphoid tissue and promotes intestinal immune homeostasis
